Grid of pathway enrichment across comparisons

Source: R/enrichment_plots.R
plot_enrichment_grid.Rd

Shows gene sets (rows) across comparisons (columns), e.g. the Hallmark sets across cell types: colour is the normalized enrichment score (GSEA) or -log10 adjusted p-value (over-representation), size the -log10 adjusted p-value or the number of genes, and non-significant results are faded. For the top gene sets of one or a few results, see plot_enrichment_dots.

Usage

plot_enrichment_grid(
  enrichment,
  terms = NULL,
  n = 5,
  fill = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  padj.cutoff = 0.05,
  significance = c("fade", "grey", "hide"),
  size.max = NULL,
  cluster.terms = TRUE,
  term.replace = NULL,
  wrap.width = 40,
  cols = NULL,
  flip = FALSE,
  cell.width = 0.18,
  cell.height = 0.18,
  legend.position = c("right", "left", "top", "bottom", "none"),
  bg = "transparent",
  ...
)

Arguments

enrichment

Results of standardize_enrichment, or anything it reads (a table, a clusterProfiler result, or a named list of them, one per comparison)

terms

Gene sets to show (names after cleaning, or the original `term_id`s): a character vector, or a named list (groups of rows). If NULL (default), the `n` most significant of each comparison, combined

n

Number of top gene sets per comparison when `terms` is NULL, default is 5

fill

What the colour shows: "nes" or "padj" (-log10 adjusted p-value). If NULL (default), "nes" when the results have NES (GSEA), else "padj"

size

What the dot size shows: "padj" (-log10 adjusted p-value), "count" or "gene_ratio". If NULL (default), "padj" when colour shows NES, else "count"

padj.cutoff

Adjusted p-value below which a result is significant, default is 0.05

significance

"fade" (default; significant dots opaque with a dark ring, the others faded), "grey" (non-significant dots grey) or "hide"

size.max

Value drawn as the largest dot (larger values are drawn at that size). If NULL (default), 10 for -log10 adjusted p-values, else the largest value

cluster.terms

Whether to order gene sets by hierarchical clustering of their colour values across comparisons (within their groups), default is TRUE. Otherwise in the order given, or by the first comparison's value

term.replace

Replacements in gene set names, applied after cleaning: a named character vector of regular expressions and their replacements, e.g. `c("Extracellular matrix" = "ECM")`. Default is NULL

wrap.width

Gene set names are wrapped onto lines of at most this many characters, default is 40

cols

Colours of the colour scale: NULL (default; "blue-magenta" for NES, "seq-purple" for -log10 adjusted p-values), a palette name or colours from low to high

flip

Whether to draw comparisons as rows and gene sets as columns, default is FALSE

cell.width, cell.height

Width of a column and height of a row in inches, default is 0.18

legend.position

Position of the legends, default is "right"

bg

Background colour, default is "transparent"

...

Arguments to standardize_enrichment when `enrichment` is not standardized yet (e.g. `comparison.col`)

Value

A ggplot object; its source data (export_source_data) are the plotted rows of the standardized table

See also

plot_enrichment_dots, plot_enrichment_bars, standardize_enrichment

Examples

set.seed(1)
sets <- paste0("HALLMARK_SET_", 1:12)
gsea <- function() data.frame(pathway = sets, pval = runif(12)^3, NES = rnorm(12, sd = 1.5),
                              size = 100)
res <- lapply(list(A = gsea(), B = gsea(), C = gsea()), function(d) {
    d$padj <- p.adjust(d$pval, "BH")
    d
})
plot_enrichment_grid(res, n = 4)
